Fine-tune the axes drawn along a spiral

Source: R/scale-spiral-axis.R
scale_spiral_axis.Rd

scale_x_spiral_axis() and scale_y_spiral_axis() are ordinary continuous scales that additionally carry the settings of the axis which coord_spiral() paints along the spiral: where the axis sits, how long its ticks are and how its labels are turned.

Usage

scale_x_spiral_axis(
  ...,
  discrete = FALSE,
  axis_at = NULL,
  tick_length = 0.007,
  label_rot = NULL,
  label_size = NULL,
  show = TRUE
)

scale_y_spiral_axis(
  ...,
  side = c("end", "start", "both"),
  axis_at = NULL,
  tick_length = 0.008,
  label_rot = NULL,
  label_size = NULL,
  max_labels = NULL,
  show = TRUE
)

Arguments

...

Passed on to ggplot2::scale_x_continuous() / ggplot2::scale_x_discrete() or ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(), for example breaks, minor_breaks, labels, limits or trans. minor_breaks draws the short unlabelled ticks between two breaks; the coord paints them at 55% of tick_length, and minor_breaks = NULL leaves them out.

discrete

Use a discrete scale instead of a continuous one, for a factor or character x aesthetic (one violin or box per category). Only scale_x_spiral_axis() needs it; breaks then takes the category values.

axis_at

Put the radial (y) ruler at a fixed direction instead, in degrees measured counter-clockwise from the east (right) direction: 0 is right, 90 top, 180 left. The last crossing of that direction on the outermost turn is used. NULL keeps the side behaviour. Ignored by scale_x_spiral_axis(), whose axis runs at every break along the spiral.

tick_length

Length of the ticks, in npc units (the panel is 1 x 1). Use 0 to hide the ticks. The coord shortens the ticks (and keeps the labels just outside them) so that both stay inside the white gap between two neighbouring turns, whatever height / gap is.

label_rot

Rotation of the labels in degrees. NULL (the default) turns every label along the spiral, so it follows the arc; a number turns all labels by that fixed angle, e.g. 90 for always-vertical labels.

label_size

Text size in points. NULL inherits axis.text.x / axis.text.y from the theme.

show

Draw this axis at all? FALSE hides the ticks and labels while keeping the data, which is handy for facets where the axis is redundant.

side

Where the radial (y) ruler is drawn: at the "start" of the spiral, at its "end" (the default) or on "both" sides, exactly like the side argument of spiralize::spiral_yaxis(). Every tick is a short segment that runs along the spiral, and its label is turned to the tangent at that point, so it reads along the arc and never ends up upside down. Only used by scale_y_spiral_axis(); ignored when axis_at is given.

max_labels

Maximum number of radial labels kept when the track is too thin for all the breaks. NULL keeps every break. Only used by scale_y_spiral_axis().

Value

A ggplot2 scale that also carries the spiral axis settings.

Details

Use them exactly like ggplot2::scale_x_continuous() / ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(); breaks, minor_breaks, labels, limits, trans, ... keep their usual meaning, so the ticks shown on the spiral are the breaks of the scale.

Both axes size themselves against the white gap between two turns: the ticks are shortened to fit, the labels sit just outside them, and the number of radial labels follows the thickness of the track and the height of the device. Nothing has to be tuned by hand, but every piece can still be overridden through the arguments below.

Examples

library(ggplot2)
d <- data.frame(x = seq(0, 1, length.out = 200),
                y = sin(seq(0, 1, length.out = 200) * 6 * pi) * .35 + .5)

ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_spiral_axis(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = .1), label_size = 6) +
  scale_y_spiral_axis(breaks = c(.3, .5, .7), axis_at = 0, label_rot = 90) +
  coord_spiral()
#> Error in scale_x_spiral_axis(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1), label_size = 6): could not find function "scale_x_spiral_axis"
